scope: Concentrate precious-metal ore into a few rare, rich lodes for newly initialized natural-resource reservoirs.

behavior.lodes: Three to five seed-selected, non-overlapping prospects, subject to available accessible land.
behavior.placement: Broad geological prospect scores favor accessible uplands; a compact radial profile leaves barren ground between lodes.
behavior.scale: Radius is proportional to the shorter map extent; increasing world size preserves a few coherent districts rather than multiplying deposits.
behavior.richness: Reference core grades are 1.5–2.5, giving 18,000–30,000 opening tonnes at lode centres. There is no world-average renormalization.
behavior.accounting: Existing extraction, finite reserves, depletion, owned inventories and payment rules remain binding. Geology never consumes simulation randomness.
behavior.persistence: New reservoirs carry geology revision 2. Already-saved unmarked reservoirs retain their original opening geography, positions and depletion rather than being redistributed or rejected.

surveyQualification: Five declared seeds at Regional scale, three continents and four states. This measures static geography, not historical economic calibration or long-run precious-metal prices.

checks.environment: Shared workspace and an isolated archive with only this geological change and its tests.

checks.command: node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=2 tests/precious-deposits.test.ts tests/natural-resources.test.ts tests/extended-economy.test.ts tests/productive-facilities.test.ts
checks.qualification: The isolated equivalent also excludes unrelated investment, politics and population edits.
Test concurrency was limited to two with a temporary Node launcher, runner timeouts and a three-minute process-group bound. This is not a full-suite pass.

checks.command: node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='regional, continental and world geography' tests/precious-deposits.test.ts
checks.environment: Previous committed geology with the new regression test.

checks.check: Synthetic saved world produced by the previous implementation restores with identical resource reservoirs under the new code.
Browser preview of precious-metal ore at 1440×1000 shows three compact deposits with mostly barren land; no page errors.

refinement.design: The existing source field remains canonical for mining, map quantities and save validation. Saved opening geology is fixed, while new-world calibration is explicit.
refinement.functions: Reviewed stable prospect ranking, seed-only grades, bounded exclusion, radial support, accessible-land filtering, initialization and revision validation.
refinement.performance: At most five linear candidate scans and bounded local painting once per cached geography. The temporary score array is released; capacity queries remain O(1). A deterministic 100,000-query contract proves repeated quotes do not revisit terrain.

benchmark.workload: Three trials on synthetic 8,064- and 129,024-cell fields; median initial lookup and 100,000 cached lookups. Concurrent validation and JIT warmup make these diagnostic timings, not throughput comparisons.

refinement.documentation: Domain comments explain rare rich centres, non-overlap, absence of endowment renormalization, caching and fixed saved geology. The supply-chain guide states the new-world scope.
